propositions.text: The appellant is a Montenegrin citizen who alleges he is gay and was victimized due to his sexual orientation.
propositions.quote: He is a citizen of Montenegro and alleges that he is gay. He alleges that he was the victim of violence and discrimination due to his sexual orientation

propositions.text: The appellant claims police did not assist him when he requested help and fled to Canada claiming refugee status.
propositions.quote: and that the police did not assist him when he requested assistance. He fled to Canada and claimed refugee status.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the appellant is a Montenegrin gay man alleging violence and police non-assistance, who fled to Canada claiming refugee status.

propositions.text: The RPD found inconsistencies in the appellant's testimony about when he first fell in love with a man.
propositions.quote: He testified that his first fell in love with a man in 2007 but in his basis of claim (BOC) form, he first never mentioned this. In an amended BOC he stated that this took place three years later in 2010;

propositions.text: The RPD found the appellant claimed to have asked police for help but his BOC forms state he never did.
propositions.quote: He testified that he asked police for help on three occasions but in both versions of his BOC he states he never asked the police for assistance;

propositions.text: The RPD found no corroborative evidence of the appellant's sexual orientation.
propositions.quote: The Appellant provided no corroborative evidence of his sexual orientation;

propositions.text: The RPD found state protection adequate in Montenegro and the appellant's allegations of seeking police help not credible.
propositions.quote: State protection is adequate in Montenegro and the Appellant's own allegations of seeking police assistance are not credible.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found inconsistencies in appellant's testimony, no corroboration of sexual orientation, and adequate state protection in Montenegro.

propositions.text: The appellant appeals to the RAD to be recognized as a refugee or person in need of protection or for redetermination by the RPD.
propositions.quote: The Appellant has appealed this decision and is now asking the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) to recognize him as a Convention refugee or a person in need of protection. In the alternative, he asks that this matter be referred back to the RPD for redetermination.

propositions.text: The appellant requests to submit new evidence but none is in the record and requests an oral hearing.
propositions.quote: While the Appellant requests to submit new evidence, no new evidence is contained in his Appellant's record. He also requests an oral hearing.

propositions.text: The appellant argues the RPD wrongly expected proof of sexuality through evidence of a same-sex relationship.
propositions.quote: The RPD erroneously expected the Appellant to prove his sexuality through evidence of a same-sex relationship

propositions.text: The RPD failed to consider the appellant's background regarding LGBT involvement and same-sex activity.
propositions.quote: The RPD failed to consider the Appellant's background when considering his involvement with the LGBT community and his same-sex activity;

propositions.text: The RPD failed to consider the appellant's gender or sexual orientation category affecting credibility and state protection analysis.
propositions.quote: The RPD failed to consider which gender or sexual orientation category the Appellant fell into and this could have impacted its credibility and state protection analysis;

propositions.text: The appellant did not mention when he first fell in love with a man in original BOC because he thought only problems faced needed description.
propositions.quote: The Appellant did not mention when he first fell in love with another man in his original BOC because he thought he only had to describe the problems he faced;

propositions.text: The RPD breached procedural fairness by requiring the appellant to conduct hearing via videoconference.
propositions.quote: The RPD breached procedural fairness by requiring the Appellant to conduct his hearing via videoconference.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant appeals to RAD, argues RPD errors on evidence and fairness, requests oral hearing but submits no new evidence.

propositions.text: The decision-maker considered and applied the Chairperson's Guideline 9 on proceedings involving sexual orientation and gender identity.
propositions.quote: I have considered and applied the Chairperson's Guideline 9: Proceedings Before the IRB Involving Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity and Expression (SOGIE guidelines).

paragraphs.summary: The court considered and applied the Chairperson's Guideline 9 on sexual orientation and gender identity proceedings.

propositions.text: The appeal is dismissed; the appellant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.
propositions.quote: I dismiss the appeal. The RPD was correct in finding that the Appellant is neither a Convention refugee, nor a person in need of protection.

propositions.text: The appellant is accepted as a gay man on a balance of probabilities.
propositions.quote: I accept, on a balance of probabilities, that the Appellant is a gay man.

propositions.text: The appellant has not established that he sought police protection.
propositions.quote: However, I find that the Appellant has not established that he ever reached out to the police for protection.

propositions.text: Montenegrin authorities would adequately protect the appellant if he returned.
propositions.quote: I further find that the Montenegrin authorities would be able to protect him adequately as a gay man if he were to return.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal, accepts appellant is gay, finds no police protection sought, and adequate protection in Montenegro.

propositions.text: The RAD must determine if oral hearing requirements under IRPA s.110(6) are met, including admissible new evidence.
propositions.quote: According to the case law, the RAD must determine whether the requirements for an oral hearing set out in subsection 110(6) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA) have been met.

propositions.text: One factor is that new evidence on appeal must be admissible.
propositions.quote: One of the determining factors is that new evidence presented on appeal must have been found to be admissible.

propositions.text: The appellant submitted no new evidence.
propositions.quote: The Appellant has not submitted any new evidence.

propositions.text: The request for an oral hearing is denied due to no new evidence.
propositions.quote: As there is no new evidence to be analyzed in a hearing before the RAD, the request is denied.

paragraphs.summary: The court denies oral hearing request because no new admissible evidence was submitted.

propositions.text: The court's role is to review all evidence and decide if the RPD decision was correct.
propositions.quote: My role is to look at all the evidence and decide if the RPD made the correct decision.

propositions.text: There was no procedural fairness breach from conducting the RPD hearing via videoconference.
propositions.quote: There is no breach of procedural fairness that resulted from conducting the RPD hearing via videoconference

paragraphs.summary: The court states its role to review evidence and finds no procedural fairness breach from videoconference hearing.

propositions.text: The appellant argues the RPD breached procedural fairness by requiring videoconference hearing.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues that the RPD breached procedural fairness by requiring the Appellant to conduct the hearing via videoconference.

propositions.text: Videoconferencing is accepted technology respecting procedural fairness principles.
propositions.quote: Videoconferencing is an accepted technology that generally respects the principles of procedural fairness.

propositions.text: The hearing was conducted respectfully, giving appellant ample opportunity to present evidence and know the case.
propositions.quote: I have reviewed the hearing which was conducted respectfully and gave the Appellant ample opportunity to present oral evidence, make representations and know the case to be met.

propositions.text: There was no procedural fairness breach from the videoconference hearing.
propositions.quote: I find that there was no breach in procedural fairness resulting from the fact that the hearing was conducted via videoconference.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues procedural fairness breach from videoconference; court finds no breach and hearing was fair.

propositions.text: To get refugee status, claimant must show clear and convincing evidence that state cannot protect them adequately.
propositions.quote: In order to be granted refugee status, a claimant must demonstrate through clear and convincing evidence that the state in their country of origin is unable to protect them adequately.

propositions.text: Claimants generally must show they made reasonable efforts to seek state protection.
propositions.quote: Claimants are generally required to demonstrate that they made reasonable efforts to seek state protection.

propositions.text: The appellant did not make reasonable efforts to seek state protection and Montenegro offers adequate protection as a gay man.
propositions.quote: For the reasons that follow, I find that the Appellant did not make reasonable efforts to seek state protection and that the Montenegrin state offers him adequate protection as a gay man.

paragraphs.summary: The court states refugee status requires showing state protection failure and finds appellant did not seek protection and Montenegro offers adequate protection.

propositions.text: The RPD found appellant did not reasonably explain why he omitted seeking state protection in BOC forms.
propositions.quote: The RPD found that the Appellant did not reasonably explain why he did not mention his attempts at seeking state protection in either his original or his amended BOC.

propositions.text: The appellant did not contest the RPD finding about omission explanation.
propositions.quote: The Appellant did not contest this finding

propositions.text: The court agrees appellant has not established he sought police assistance.
propositions.quote: and I agree with it. I find that the Appellant has not established that he sought assistance from the police.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found appellant did not explain omission of seeking protection; appellant did not contest; court agrees no police assistance was established.

propositions.text: In original BOC, appellant said he did not seek police help because police would not help him.
propositions.quote: In the Appellant's original BOC, he was directly asked if he had sought protection or assistance from any authorities including the police and he said he did not because he knew the police would not help him.

propositions.text: In amended BOC, appellant repeated he never asked police for help for similar reasons.
propositions.quote: In his amended BOC, he repeated that he never asked the police for help for similar reasons.

propositions.text: At hearing, appellant testified he asked police for help three times but they refused.
propositions.quote: However, in his hearing he testifies to asking the police for help on three occasions and that they refused to help him.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found appellant said in BOCs he never sought police help but testified at hearing he did ask police three times.

propositions.text: The RPD found appellant's explanation that interpreter erred is not reasonable.
propositions.quote: I agree with the RPD that the Appellant explanation for this inconsistency, that the interpreter must have made a mistake, is not reasonable.

propositions.text: Appellant signed original BOC as true and accurate and repeated answer in amended BOC.
propositions.quote: He signed the original BOC, stating that it was complete true and accurate. He also had an opportunity to provide this information in his amended BOC but instead, he repeated his answer that he did not seek help from the police as they would not help him.

propositions.text: Appellant stated in Port of Entry interview he did not seek police assistance.
propositions.quote: I also note that he stated in a Port of Entry interview that he did not seek police assistance.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees with RPD that appellant's interpreter error explanation is unreasonable; appellant signed BOCs and said no police help sought.

propositions.text: On balance of probabilities, appellant never sought police or authority protection regarding sexual orientation incidents.
propositions.quote: I find, on a balance of probabilities, that the Appellant never sought protection or assistance from the police or any other authorities in relation to incidents or violence involving his sexual orientation.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellant likely never sought police or authority protection for incidents related to his sexual orientation.

propositions.text: Country documents show mixed treatment of LGBT individuals in Montenegro with discrimination and harassment.
propositions.quote: The country documentation relating to the treatment of LGBT individuals in Montenegro is mixed. LGBT individuals face discrimination and harassment from the population.

propositions.text: Some public LGBT activists faced violence but visibility and police support have increased.
propositions.quote: Some public LGBT activists and figures have faced violence. That being said, there is an increasing trend towards greater visibility of LGBT individuals in everyday life, every police station has an officer dedicated to serving this population and NGOs are working with the police to foster better communication and trust between LGBT individuals and the police.

propositions.text: Police have arrested and charged perpetrators of violence against LGBT individuals; Ombudsman reports fewer complaints.
propositions.quote: there were multiple examples of the police efficiently and effectively arresting and charging perpetrators of violent attacks against LGBT individuals. The Ombudsman's Office received and investigated a number of complaints from LGBT individuals and reported a drop in the number of complaints. In 2016, the Office only received three complaints of discrimination based on sexual orientation.

paragraphs.summary: Country documents show mixed treatment of LGBT in Montenegro but increasing visibility, police support, and fewer complaints.

propositions.text: A 2012 report claims institutions cannot protect LGBT rights but court gives it less weight than recent reports.
propositions.quote: I note that one report submitted by the Appellant before the RPD states that institutions and authorities are incapable of protecting the rights of LGBT people in Montenegro, but this report is from 2012 and I place less weight on it than on the more recent reports cited above.

propositions.text: Court prefers recent reports due to improvements in LGBT protections in last ten years in Montenegro.
propositions.quote: I prefer the more recent articles because many improvements in protecting LGBT individuals have taken place in the last ten years in Montenegro.

paragraphs.summary: The court gives less weight to a 2012 report and prefers recent reports showing improvements in LGBT protections in Montenegro.

propositions.text: Despite areas for improvement, there is adequate state protection for appellant in his circumstances.
propositions.quote: While there are still areas for improvement in terms of protections for LGBT individuals in Montenegro, I find that there is adequate state protection for the Appellant in his specific circumstances.

propositions.text: Appellant was never a public figure or activist and has no such ambition.
propositions.quote: I note that he was never a public figure or activist and has never stated that he has this ambition.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds adequate state protection for appellant who is not a public figure or activist.

propositions.text: Appellant alleges involvement in fight due to being gay, leading to charge and conditional sentence, police hate gay people.
propositions.quote: The Appellant alleged that he was involved in a fight with a group of young men who were bad-mouthing him because he is gay. He alleges that the incident led to him being charged and receiving a conditional sentence because the police hate gay people.

propositions.text: Appellant did not seek police help but police got involved as fight escalated.
propositions.quote: He did not seek police assistance, but they got involved as the fight got worse.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant alleges a fight due to his sexual orientation led to charges and police hatred, but he did not seek police help.

propositions.text: RPD noted appellant defended himself with broken bottle, leading to charge and sentence.
propositions.quote: The RPD noted in the hearing that the Appellant mentioned that he defended himself with a broken bottle which may have led to him being charged and sentenced.

propositions.text: RPD concluded arrest and sentencing due to weapon use, not discrimination or harassment by police.
propositions.quote: The RPD concluded that his arrest and sentencing was due to him using a bottle as a weapon rather than due to any discrimination or harassment from the police related to his sexual orientation.

propositions.text: Court agrees with RPD conclusion; appellant did not contest it.
propositions.quote: I agree. The Appellant did not contest this conclusion.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD and court find appellant's arrest and sentence due to weapon use, not police discrimination; appellant did not contest.

propositions.text: Appellant acknowledged weapon use might have influenced arrest and sentencing.
propositions.quote: While the Appellant states that he was arrested and sentenced because he was gay, he acknowledged that he used the bottle as a weapon and that this might have influenced the result.

propositions.text: No evidence of police discrimination or mistreatment of LGBT individuals in charging and sentencing patterns.
propositions.quote: there is no evidence of discrimination or mistreatment of LGBT individuals by the police force and the justice system in the patterns of charging and sentencing in the country documentation.

propositions.text: Appellant provided no evidence to corroborate his version of the incident.
propositions.quote: The Appellant has also provided no evidence to corroborate his version of this incident.

propositions.text: Court finds incident does not show harassment or discrimination by authorities against appellant.
propositions.quote: Given the country documentation, the Appellant's own concession and the lack of any evidence to show otherwise, I find that this incident does not represent an example of harassment or discrimination by authorities against the Appellant.

propositions.text: Court has credibility concerns about appellant's contradictory testimony about police interactions.
propositions.quote: I have credibility concerns discussed above in relation to the Appellant's contradictory testimony about his interactions with authorities and find that the presumption of truthfulness has been rebutted.

propositions.text: Credibility issues influenced conclusion about police interaction allegations.
propositions.quote: This credibility issue has also been relevant in reaching my conclusion as to this interaction with the police as they involve similar allegations.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no evidence of police discrimination, notes appellant's credibility issues, and rejects his harassment claims.

propositions.text: To conclude on state protection adequacy, court considers if appellant made reasonable efforts to seek protection.
propositions.quote: In coming to my conclusion as to whether there is adequate state protection for the Appellant, I am to consider if he made reasonable efforts to seek state protection.

propositions.text: The appellant did not make reasonable efforts to seek state protection as he did not establish seeking it.
propositions.quote: I find that he did not. As discussed above, he has not established that he ever sought state protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellant did not make reasonable efforts to seek state protection as he never established seeking it.

propositions.text: Authorities have made great strides in offering operationally effective protection to LGBT individuals in Montenegro.
propositions.quote: It is clear from the country documentation that authorities have made great strides in offering operationally effective protection to LGBT individuals.

propositions.text: Protection would be reasonably forthcoming for the Appellant if he sought state protection.
propositions.quote: I find that protection would be reasonably forthcoming for the Appellant if he were to seek state protection.

propositions.text: Discrimination and harassment from the general population persists but it is not reasonable that the Appellant did not try to seek protection from state authorities.
propositions.quote: While discrimination and harassment from the general population does persist, it is not reasonable that the Appellant did not even try to seek protection from state authorities who have demonstrated that they take incidents of discrimination, harassment and violence against LGBT individuals seriously.

propositions.text: Adequate state protection exists for the Appellant in Montenegro.
propositions.quote: Adequate state protection exists for the Appellant in Montenegro

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Montenegro authorities offer effective protection to LGBT individuals, protection would be forthcoming for the Appellant, and adequate state protection exists.

propositions.text: There is adequate state protection in Montenegro for the Appellant who identifies as gay.
propositions.quote: In conclusion, there is adequate state protection in Montenegro for the Appellant who identifies as gay.

propositions.text: The Appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.
propositions.quote: For this reason, he is neither a Convention refugee, nor a person in need of protection.

propositions.text: Other arguments and conclusions are not determinative.
propositions.quote: Other arguments and conclusions not determinative

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes adequate state protection exists, so the Appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor in need of protection; other arguments are not determinative.

propositions.text: The RPD failed to determine his specific gender identity or sexual orientation.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues without merit that the RPD failed to determine his specific gender identity or sexual orientation.

propositions.text: The Appellant identifies as a gay man in his BOC and amended BOC, confirmed by the RPD at the hearing.
propositions.quote: The Appellant identifies himself specifically as a gay man in his BOC and his amended BOC and this identity was confirmed by the RPD at the hearing.

propositions.text: There is no basis to the argument that his specific identity was not canvassed and identified correctly by the RPD.
propositions.quote: There is no basis to the argument that his specific identity was not canvassed and identified correctly by the RPD.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues the RPD failed to determine his gender identity, but the court finds the RPD correctly identified his identity as a gay man.

propositions.text: The RPD was overly focused on same-sex relationships and involvement in the gay community to determine if he was gay.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues that the RPD was overly focused on his same-sex relationships and his involvement in the gay community in determining whether he was gay.

propositions.text: The RPD expected corroborative evidence without analyzing explanations for lack of such evidence, an error under SOGIE guidelines.
propositions.quote: The RPD does appear to have expected corroborative evidence of the Appellant's sexual orientation through support letters from ex-partners and community groups without analysing his explanations for not having this evidence. I agree with the Appellant that this is an error under the SOGIE guidelines.

propositions.text: The court accepts the Appellant is gay on a balance of probabilities and focuses on state protection, so the error is not determinative.
propositions.quote: However, I have focused on state protection in this decision and have accepted that the Appellant is gay on a balance of probabilities, so this error is not determinative of this appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues the RPD erred by focusing on corroborative evidence; the court agrees but accepts the Appellant is gay and finds the error not determinative.

propositions.text: The appeal is dismissed and the RPD decision is confirmed that the Appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.
propositions.quote: I dismiss the appeal and confirm the decision of the RPD that the Appellant is neither a Convention refugee, nor a person in need of protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal and confirms the RPD decision that the Appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor in need of protection.
